purpose: What the filings of the corpus say about a syndicate's own run-off, year by year (the author's decision of 1 October 2026, option A; round 62, fourth cycle). One entry per syndicate-year whose filing says that the syndicate itself is in run-off or has stopped, or will stop, underwriting, in whatever words it uses (some filings, Syndicate 1209's among them, never say run-off). The whole-year run-off rule reads the WHOLE entries; the others are kept so that every reading is on record and a reader can see what was not counted, and why. An entry is classified only as far as the filing's words go: where they do not settle it the entry is NOTCOUNT and its note says so. A legacy vehicle (a syndicate that takes on other syndicates' liabilities by reinsurance to close or loss portfolio transfer) that says it is in run-off is WHOLE like any other; whether the analysis keeps it is for the analysis's assumed-business regime, not for this register.

categories.WHOLE: the filing states that the syndicate is in run-off, or has ceased underwriting, from the start of the year or before: a run-off year
categories.PART: the run-off begins during the year (runoff_from says when): the syndicate was underwriting for part of it
categories.AFTER: the run-off begins at or after the year end: the syndicate was underwriting during the year
categories.NOTCOUNT: not counted as a run-off year: the filing's words do not settle it (the note says why), or the statement is about another entity

scope: What is complete, and how that was checked. (1) By test: every filing of the corpus (the 1,065 committed extraction records) is scanned with the statement forms in scripts/runoff_statement_forms.py, the forms in which a filing says that its syndicate is in run-off, has stopped underwriting or will stop. A filing that a form matches is an entry here, or the record reviewed apart (reviewed_not_run_off), or its matching sentences are listed in scan_reviewed with the reason each is not the syndicate's own run-off (another entity, a class or line, an office or channel, or not a stop); tests/test_runoff_corpus_register.py fails if a matching sentence is in none of them. For those forms, then, the WHOLE, PART and AFTER entries are complete over the whole corpus. (2) Not by test: the first version of this register, built from filings that say run-off or ceased underwriting, missed 17 syndicate-years that the forms find. The independent review of 1 October 2026 found ten of them (Syndicate 1209's 2015 to 2017 filings, which never say run-off, and seven others in the working sample), its verifier two more (779/2016 and 3500/2015), and the forms five more (1882/2016, 2008/2021, 3330/2017, 6132/2021 and 6133/2021). (3) Keyword and pattern scans can miss oblique wording, as both 1209 years show; the forms are the defence. One entry's own words match no form (4321/2023, which says the syndicate will no longer write new follow capacity insurance business), and a statement in words that no form matches and no reader found is not in this register.
